sources.disclaimer: Internal educational summary; not legal advice; not the law of any real jurisdiction; do not cite as authority.

sources.excerpt: For gameplay, a hearing is organized around a few simplified roles: a presiding participant who keeps order and issues the outcome, a party presenting a case, a party responding to it, and witnesses who give accounts. This is a teaching abstraction, not a description of any real court's procedure or rules of evidence.
sources.notes: Non-authoritative internal educational content. 'Verified' here means the project owner checked it as original internal educational material, not that any law was verified.

sources.title: The idea of a burden of proof (internal outline)
sources.disclaimer: Internal educational summary; not legal advice; not the law of any real jurisdiction; do not cite as authority.
sources.provenance: Original internal summary created for THE BAR prototype; not official legal text. Authored by the project team to explain a general idea used in the game's scoring. No real statutory provision, judgment, case name, reporter citation or procedural rule is quoted or asserted. Reviewed internally on 2026-11-23 for educational clarity only, not for legal accuracy against any official source.
sources.excerpt: Many dispute systems expect the party making an assertion to support it. The game models this loosely: the side advancing a claim is asked to connect it to the information available, and the response is tested against that same material. The game's thresholds are invented for play and do not reproduce any real standard of proof.
sources.notes: Non-authoritative internal educational content. No real legal standard or threshold is stated or implied.

sources.excerpt: In the game a witness is first asked to give an account and then to answer questions from the opposing side. The two-stage structure is a simplified mechanic for pacing and scoring; it is not a statement of how examination is conducted in any real court, and no real rule of evidence is applied.

sources.excerpt: The game asks players to finish with a brief outcome that states what they decided and why, pointing to the material they relied on.
